To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transplantation of NGF-producing neural stem cells to the striatum protects the GABAergic projection neurons and the cholinergic interneurons of the striatum against the excitotoxic damage caused by the injection of quininic acid, 1 week later, and that this protective effect is mediated by an indirect mechanism that involves a substantial reduction of astroglial and of microglial reactions in the host striatal tissue.

(i) NGF-producing neural stem cells protect the striatum against excitotoxic damage; (ii) the protection is due to an indirect effect mediated by a reduction in the host response to the excitotoxic injury; (iii) the effect is specific to the NGF-transfected cells, and is not observed with the control cells or the BDNF-transduced cells; (iv) the protective effect is long-lasting; (v) the protection is observed in both projection neurons and stri

genetically engineered, NGF-producing neural stem cells are capable of rescuing the striatal projection neurons against excitotoxic degeneration and preventing the development of reactive gliosis, and that these effects are mediated by a mechanism that does not involve direct contact of the transplanted cells with the target cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of stem cell transplantation to protect the striatum against neurodegeneration, which is a common feature of several neurodegenerative disorders.
the application of neural stem cells as a means to prevent the development of degenerative diseases in the central nervous system.
the use of genetically manipulated neural stem cells for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NGF-producing neural stem cells are a highly effective means of protection against the neurodegeneration induced by excitotoxic lesions of the striatum.

the NGF-producing neural stem cell grafts are able to protect striatal projection neurons and cholinergic interneurons against excitotoxic damage and that this protection is mediated by a reduction in the glial reaction in response to the toxin.
the NGF-transfected stem cells are more efficient at rescuing striatal neurons than the BDNF-transfected cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of genetically engineered neural stem cells producing NGF or BDNF can prevent the degeneration of the projection neurons in the lesioned striatum, and this effect is mediated by the protection of the host striatum from excitotoxicity.
we have shown that NGF-transduced neural stem cells can protect the striatum against the degenerative effects of quinolin acid-induced excitotoxicity.
the use of neural stem cells genetically engineered to secrete neurotrophic factors may represent a promising approach to treat neurodegenerative disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the transplantation of genetically modified neural cells producing NGF or BDNF to the striatum is able to counteract the excitotoxin-induced neuronal degeneration in this area, and that the NGF-producing cells appear to be particularly effective.
genetically engineered stem cells are a very powerful tool to treat neurological disorders.
NGF-producing neural stem cells have a protective effect on the striatum, which is superior to that exerted by BDNF-producing cells.
